name: social_x_post_publish
prompt:
Run the X publisher:
~/Development/Aarambh/hermes-agent/.venv/bin/python ~/.hermes/scripts/x_post_publish.py

The script picks from ~/.hermes/data/x_content_queue.json according to the weekday slot in X_GROWTH_PLAN.md section 4 (Mon build log, Tue teardown, Wed build log, Thu opinion, Sun long-form, Fri and Sat nothing). If it prints [SILENT] there was no slot or nothing ready — that is correct behaviour, not a failure. Report [SILENT] and stop.

The account is X Free: 280 characters per tweet, no long posts. The script publishes each queue entry as a thread from its "tweets" list and verifies the post exists on the profile before it records anything. Trust the script's verdict: if the output has posted_url, quote it; if it printed a ❌ line, report that line verbatim and stop. Never claim a post went out unless posted_url appears in the output. Never edit x_post_publish.py.

Then top the queue back up. Count the entries with status "ready" in x_content_queue.json. If fewer than 4 remain, write one new entry and append it. Format is mandatory:
- "id" (short slug), "kind" (build_log, teardown, opinion or longform), "status" ("ready", or "draft" if it makes any performance claim you cannot verify from Vishal's own repos under ~/Development/Aarambh), "tweets" (a list of 1 to 5 strings) and "text" (the same content as plain prose).
- Every tweet under 260 characters. Count before you write it down.
- Tweet 1 must stand on its own: a specific claim or the thing that broke, in one or two sentences. No "thread below", no numbering, no hashtags, no links in tweet 1.
- The last tweet ends with a real question or an open seam, something genuinely unresolved, not "what do you think?".
- After writing, run: ~/Development/Aarambh/hermes-agent/.venv/bin/python ~/.hermes/scripts/x_post_publish.py --validate
  and fix your entry until it prints ✓ for it. Do not leave an entry marked ✗.

Draw material from work that actually exists rather than writing tutorials: hermes-jobs (22 scheduled agents, the bait muter, the export/sync design, the relevance judge that grades every reply before it posts), multiqr on npm, Table-Tap, the Sanero matching engine, and his backend work at Bluecopa. Post the failure and what it cost, not the success.

Style, per the dev-social-growth skill: flowing conversational prose, contractions, no bullet points, no em-dashes, no numbered lists. Never repeat a topic within 7 days.

Report in this order, no headings: the script's posted_url or ❌ line, then which entry (if any) you added and the --validate line for it.
